appearance-sub: Control how Maximal appears on your desktop.
appearance-dock-label: {os, select, macos {Always show in Dock} other {Always show in taskbar}}
appearance-dock-sub: {os, select, macos {Keep Maximal in the Dock even when the window is closed. Right-click the Dock icon for quick actions.} other {Keep Maximal in the taskbar even when the window is closed.}}
account-requirement-sub: Maximal forwards requests through your own Copilot license. {plansLink}.
account-unauth-body: Sign in with the GitHub account that holds your Copilot subscription. Until you do, the proxy accepts connections but rejects Copilot calls.
account-pending-body: We’ll copy your sign-in code and open GitHub for you. Paste the code on the GitHub page to finish.
account-roster-sub: Other accounts saved on this {os, select, macos {Mac} other {computer}}. Switching restarts the proxy signed in as that account.
account-switch-different: Sign in as a different account
account-rosters-divider: or use an account you already know
account-remembered-sub: Accounts you’ve signed into before on this {os, select, macos {Mac} other {computer}}. Picking one restarts the proxy signed in as that account.
account-gh-reuse-sub: Sign in with an account you’re already logged into with {ghCode} on this {os, select, macos {Mac} other {computer}} — no code to copy.
account-confirm-sign-out: Sign out? The proxy will restart and stop forwarding Copilot requests until you sign in again.
account-confirm-remove: Remove {login}? Maximal forgets its saved sign-in. This doesn’t sign you out of gh or GitHub in the browser.
account-err-gh-use-generic: Couldn’t sign in with that account. Try the code-based sign-in above.
account-err-gh-use-authless: Signed in as {login}, but the proxy came back unauthenticated — that account may not have Copilot access on this host.
account-err-gh-use-no-restart: Sign-in didn’t complete — the proxy may not have restarted. Try again, or use the code-based sign-in above.
account-err-switch-authless: Switched, but the proxy came back unauthenticated — that account’s token may no longer be valid.
account-err-switch-no-restart: Switch didn’t complete — the proxy may not have restarted. Try again.
account-rejection-explain-402: Check your Copilot plan or billing on GitHub, then try again.
account-rejection-explain-403: This model or request isn’t allowed on your current plan.
account-rejection-explain-timeout: It took too long to respond. Try again in a moment.
account-rejection-explain-429: You’ve hit a rate or quota limit. Wait a moment and try again.
account-rejection-explain-5xx: GitHub’s side returned an error. This is usually temporary — try again shortly.
account-rejection-explain-other: Try again, or check your Copilot account on GitHub.
apps-sub: One-click setup for the tools that talk to Maximal. Turn an app on and we point it at the proxy for you.
apps-install-then: Then route {appName} through Maximal. Maximal notices the install by itself; switch it on here.
apps-install-confirm-body: Maximal runs WinGet, Windows’ package manager, to download Claude Code from Anthropic and install it for your Windows account. It doesn’t ask for administrator rights. Routing stays off until you switch it on.
apps-install-running: Installing Claude Code. This can take a few minutes.
apps-install-reason-winget-missing: WinGet isn’t available on this PC, so Maximal can’t install Claude Code itself. Run the PowerShell command instead.
apps-install-reason-timed-out: The install took too long and was stopped. Try again, or run the PowerShell command in a terminal.
apps-install-reason-exit-code: WinGet stopped with exit code {code}. The output below shows why.
apps-install-reason-not-found: WinGet finished, but Claude Code isn’t found yet. Open a new terminal and run claude --version. If it still isn’t found, run the PowerShell command.
apps-install-reason-error: Maximal couldn’t finish the install. The output below may show why.
apps-conflict-existing-title: Left your existing setting in place
apps-conflict-base-url: {appName} already has a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL set by you or another tool, so Maximal didn’t change it. Remove that setting, then switch routing on again.
apps-conflict-api-key-helper: {appName} already has a custom apiKeyHelper set by you or another tool, so Maximal didn’t change it. Remove that setting, then switch routing on again.
apps-conflict-gateway-profile: {appName} is already using a gateway set up by you or another tool, so Maximal didn’t switch it. Choose a different configuration in {appName}, then switch routing on again.
apps-conflict-cleanup-detail: Maximal stopped routing {appName}, but preserved settings changed after setup. Review the app’s settings and manually remove the Maximal routing entry before trying again.
apps-codex-shared-setting: CLI and Desktop share one setting.
apps-codex-restart-session: After changes, restart Codex and start a new local session.
apps-codex-settings-unchanged: Model, review, approval, and sandbox settings stay unchanged.
apps-codex-settings-precedence: Command-line, admin, project, profile, and cloud settings may take precedence.
apps-restart-windows-body: On Windows, a Claude Code session that’s already running keeps routing through Maximal until you restart it.
apps-restart-after-disable: After disabling routing, run {exitCommand} in Claude Code and start it again for the change to take effect.
connectors-sub: Connectors give your apps tools from other services. Open one to finish its setup, choose which apps get it and which of its tools they may use.
connectors-empty-body: This version of Maximal doesn’t include any connectors.
connectors-failed-hint: Check its settings file, then switch it off and on again.
connectors-failed-hint-config: Fix its configuration below and save; it starts again with the new settings.
connectors-client-standalone-server: {client} already has its own {connector} (the “{name}” server), so Maximal doesn’t add another. Remove that one to use Maximal’s.
connectors-client-standalone-plugin: {client} already has {connector} from the “{name}” plugin, so Maximal doesn’t add another. Turn that plugin off to use Maximal’s.
connectors-endpoint-hint: For any other app that supports MCP servers, add this address as a server.
connectors-tools-sub: Choose which tools your apps can use. With Ask, you approve every call; blocked tools stay listed in your apps but are turned off.
connectors-tools-cached: Last seen {when}. Sign in to refresh.
connectors-tools-cached-off: Last seen {when}. Turn {connector} on to refresh.
connectors-tools-none: No tools yet. They appear once setup is finished.
connectors-tool-allowed-tip: Allowed: your apps can use this tool
connectors-tool-asks-tip: Asks: you approve every call (Claude Code asks you itself; other apps ask through Maximal)
connectors-tool-blocked-tip: Blocked: listed in your apps as turned off; calls are refused
connectors-config-sub: Saving restarts {connector} with the new settings.
endpoint-sub: Where Maximal listens. Use these values when wiring up a tool that isn’t in the Apps list.
endpoint-hint: The key rotates every time Maximal restarts. Use {apiKeysLink} to mint a stable, named key for long-running tools.
keys-sub: Keys that apps use to call Maximal. Add one per tool so you can tell them apart — anything not listed still works by default.
models-sub: Models available to apps through Maximal, grouped by kind. The list is fetched from the provider — refresh to pull the current catalog if a model looks missing.
models-auto-intro: Map Haiku and Sonnet aliases for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and other /v1/messages clients routed through Maximal. Choose the model used for Claude Code Auto permission checks.
models-auto-fast-hint: Used when an Anthropic Messages client requests Haiku, including background work.
models-auto-capable-hint: Used when an Anthropic Messages client requests Sonnet, including Claude Code’s opusplan.
models-auto-classifier-hint: Used by Claude Code to decide whether an action can run without asking in Auto permission mode.
models-auto-signed-out: Sign-in to retrieve the list of available models.
models-auto-fast-unavailable-title: Your Haiku alias model is no longer available
models-auto-capable-unavailable-title: Your Sonnet alias model is no longer available
models-auto-classifier-unavailable-title: Your Auto permission model is no longer available
models-auto-unavailable-detail: Choose another model or return to Automatic.
logs-sub: Daily-rotated request and handler logs, {n, plural, one {#-day} other {#-day}} retention.
logs-where-hint: Each handler writes a per-day file under the maximal state directory. Reveal the folder to inspect them, or tail the active file with {tailCmd}.
logs-retention-value: {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, then deleted on next boot
diagnostics-sub: Live state and a one-click bundle for bug reports.
diagnostics-update-apt-hint: Maximal {version} is available. To update, run this in a terminal:
diagnostics-copilot-refresh: Token will refresh on first request
uninstall-hint: This stops Maximal’s background agent, reverts any app integrations, and removes the {cliName} CLI from your PATH. You’ll drag Maximal to the Trash to finish.
uninstall-confirm:
Uninstall Maximal?

This stops the background agent and {summary}. You’ll drag the app to the Trash to finish.

This can’t be undone.
uninstall-err: Couldn’t finish uninstalling: {error}. You can run {uninstallCmd} in the terminal instead.
uninstall-complete: Maximal is uninstalled. Quit Maximal from the {os, select, macos {menu bar} other {system tray}}, then drag it from Applications to the Trash to finish.
dashboard-live-empty-detail: The live session flow will appear here when apps start sending requests through Maximal.
dashboard-live-summary: Tokens per minute over the last 15 minutes, one line per live session. {rate} tokens/min in all; {live} live, {cold} cold.
dashboard-flow-cache-hit-detail: Share of input tokens served from cache
dashboard-flow-summary: Live token flow. {rate} tokens/min in all; {live} live, {cold} cold.
dashboard-flow-other-sessions: {count, plural, one {# other session} other {# other sessions}}
sessions-empty-detail: Sessions will appear here after apps send requests through Maximal.
dashboard-sessions-client: {client, select, code {Claude Code} desktop {Claude Desktop} codex {Codex} other {Other app}}
dashboard-sessions-source-codex-catalog: the size Codex uses for this model
dashboard-sessions-source-claude-1m: the 1M window Claude Code asked for
dashboard-sessions-source-models-endpoin: the size Maximal lists for this model
dashboard-events-meta: Page {page} / {total} · {events, plural, one {# event} other {# events}}
dashboard-empty-summary: No token usage recorded for the selected period.
dashboard-empty-events: No token usage detail rows for the selected period.
dashboard-welcome-body: Usage and token-usage data will appear here as it loads.
budget-settings-sub: Whether rules are enforced, how amounts are shown, and what your provider says you have left.
budget-status-limits: {n, plural, =0 {No rules} one {# rule} other {# rules}}
budget-status-spent: {usage} of {limit} {period, select, daily {today} weekly {this week} never {in total} other {this period}}
budget-enforce-hint: When this is off, your rules are kept but nothing is refused.
budget-unit-hint: Only changes how amounts are shown. Rules are stored in AI credits.
budget-windows-hint: These figures come from the provider and can lag behind what you have spent. Rules count what Maximal records.
budget-windows-empty: Your provider hasn’t reported an allowance yet. It appears after the first request.
budget-blocked-until: Requests it covers are refused until it resets on {date} ({relative}). Raise or remove the rule to carry on.
budget-blocked-never: Requests it covers are refused until you raise or remove the rule.
budget-storage-off-body: Usage history is turned off, so every amount reads zero and no rule can be triggered.
budget-limits-sub: Caps on what Maximal will spend. A rule exists only once you add it.
budget-empty-body: Your provider bills all usage to your account. Add a rule to stop spending at an amount you choose.
budget-reset-fallback: Resets daily, {relative} ({window} hasn’t reported a reset)
budget-delete-body: “{name}” will stop applying. Spending already recorded isn’t affected.
budget-field-name-hint: Optional. Shown in the list and in the message a refused request gets.
budget-field-amount-hint: In {unit}. Typing $100 or 100 credits works too; it’s converted.
budget-field-reset-hint: Following your provider keeps the rule in step with its own reset.
budget-field-warn-hint: Percent of the rule’s amount used before it reads as nearly spent.
budget-error-amount-format: Enter an amount like {unit, select, usd {100 or $100} other {100 or 100 credits}}.
budget-error-target: Choose what the rule applies to.
budget-activity-sub-plain: What Maximal has recorded, counted from 00:00 UTC.
budget-export-failed-detail: Maximal couldn’t write the CSV where you chose. Pick another place and try again.
budget-activity-empty-body: Usage shows up here as requests go through Maximal. Try a longer range.
budget-chart-tip: {name}: {amount}, {requests, plural, one {# request} other {# requests}}, {share, number, percent}
budget-range-backwards: The last day can’t be before the first.
budget-range-incomplete: Pick both days to see that range.
budget-table-capped: Showing the first {shown} of {n} rows. The statement has every row.
native-notify-startup-body-macos: Look for the Maximal icon in your menu bar ↑
native-notify-startup-body-windows: Maximal is running. Open it from the taskbar.
native-notify-startup-body-other: Maximal is running in your system tray ↓
native-notify-signin-body: Maximal needs your GitHub Copilot account before it can serve requests. Click here — or the menu-bar icon — to open Settings and sign in.
native-notify-signin-body-windows: Maximal needs your GitHub Copilot account before it can serve requests. Open Maximal from the taskbar, then open Settings and sign in.
native-notify-failed-body: The background proxy failed to start. Click the menu-bar icon to retry startup or view the logs.
native-notify-failed-body-reason: {reason} — click the menu-bar icon to retry startup or view the logs.
native-notify-rejection-body: An upstream Copilot request was rejected. Open Settings for details.
native-notify-working-body: Your first request just went through.
native-notify-working-body-apps: Requests are going through — {apps} can use Maximal now.
native-notify-connector-connected-body: Signed in as {account}. Its tools are ready in your apps.
native-notify-connector-connected-body-n: Its tools are ready in your apps.
native-notify-connector-not-saved-body: Your system’s credential store didn’t respond, so you’ll need to sign in to {connector} again after Maximal restarts.
native-quit-body: Any apps connected to Maximal will be disconnected.
native-update-confirm-body: Maximal will download and install {version}, then restart. Requests in progress will stop.
native-update-failed-body: Maximal will open mxml.sh so you can download it there.
native-update-check-failed: Couldn’t check for updates. Check your connection and try again.
